messages.content:
Risk: Lack of Transparency
Description: Challenges in understanding or explaining the decision-making processes of AI systems, which can lead to mistrust, difficulty in enforcing compliance standards or holding relevant actors accountable for harms, and the inability to identify and correct errors.
Concern: None
Policy: Clinical Diagnosis & Treatment Recommendations

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0033055: Impaired ability to plan — Impaired ability to anticipate future events, implement instructions or goals, and develop appropriate steps ahead of time in order to carry out a task or activity. [found by 7/15 queries]
  Siblings: Impaired task monitoring, Impaired self monitoring, Impaired ability to organize
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0033071: Impaired task monitoring — Impaired ability to keep track of one's problem-solving success or failure, and to identify and correct mistakes during performance of a goal. [found by 6/15 queries]
  Siblings: Impaired ability to plan, Impaired self monitoring, Impaired ability to organize
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/Documents/Specification: specification — explicit requirement or set of requirements to be satisfied by something, such as a product, material, model, process or system [found by 12/15 queries]
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/PartiesAndSituations/SoftwareAgent: software agent — digital entity that perceives its environment and takes actions that maximize its chance of successfully achieving its goals [found by 11/15 queries]
  Siblings: automated underwriting system, automated system, party
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/Documents/Reference: reference — source that may be used to ascertain, interpret, or understand something [found by 10/15 queries]

axes.rationale: The risk of lack of transparency is directly tied to the decision-making processes of AI systems, which are software agents. Understanding who or what is making the decisions is crucial for addressing transparency concerns.

Lack of transparency can stem from unclear or insufficiently defined specifications for how the AI system should operate.  Transparent specifications are essential for understanding and evaluating AI decision-making.
